answer: Each identity grows a pearl in the shared ocean by depositing thin nacre layers of peer-verified work, one layer per epoch, each layer hash-chained to the previous one and to the epoch beacon. A layer may only be laid during a short lantern-lit tide window, when a random beacon names the tide; late or copied layers are rejected by the public ledger. A pearl earns standing only after many slow layers, so an attacker wanting a hundred fake identities must do a hundred pearls' worth of genuine work, on schedule, tide after tide, while one copied layer shatters the pearl and burns its bond.
